folder_html:
LIVE PRECIPITABLE WATER VAPOR

Column-integrated atmospheric water vapor from the operational HRRR analysis: the total water held in the full atmospheric column above each point, expressed as the depth of liquid water if it all condensed. Deep values mark moisture transport and heavy-precipitation potential in Great Lakes weather systems.

Atmospheric moisture science tracks precipitable water as the reservoir feeding clouds and precipitation. Unlike relative humidity (a near-surface saturation percentage), it integrates the whole column, revealing atmospheric rivers, lake-effect moisture plumes, and storm-system moisture transport. Units are millimeters of equivalent liquid-water depth.


Column-integrated water vapor in millimeters of equivalent liquid-water depth (HRRR PWAT analysis, fixed absolute scale): LOWEST 0 dark-blue dry column → blue → cyan → green → yellow → orange → HIGHEST+ 60 deep-purple very moist. Same moisture always shows the same color; above 60 mm clamps into deep purple. Total atmospheric-column moisture — not relative humidity.
